subject.title: Ensure transcript-to-client delivery consistency for channel-scoped sessions

question: What durable delivery-state contract should OpenClaw add for channel-scoped transcript entries: a transcript-entry ledger, an extension of delivery_queue_entries, or a separate session-state projection?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but schema ownership, adapter reconciliation semantics, idempotent redelivery policy, and Control UI/API shape are cross-boundary product and compatibility decisions that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Design Generic Ledger First
options.body: Add a SQLite-backed transcript delivery ledger tied to outbound receipts and adapter reconciliation, then surface per-entry status in session APIs and Control UI.

options.title: Limit To Queue Mitigations
options.body: Keep this issue open but accept only narrow queue-recovery mitigations until maintainers are ready to commit to the broader delivery-state surface.

options.title: Split Runtime And UI Follow-Ups
options.body: Create separate maintainer-owned runtime-ledger and Control UI/API follow-up items if the full design is too large for one implementation lane.

recommendation.title: Design Generic Ledger First
recommendation.body: Add a SQLite-backed transcript delivery ledger tied to outbound receipts and adapter reconciliation, then surface per-entry status in session APIs and Control UI.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest available history across durable outbound delivery, queue storage/recovery, SQLite migration, and related recovery hardening.
